question: In Windows 11, what does the Alt + D keyboard shortcut do in File Explorer or a web browser?

options.text: Deletes the selected file or folder

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Focuses the address bar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Alt + D keyboard shortcut** in **Windows 11** is used to focus on the **address bar** in **File Explorer** or a **web browser**.
 
• This shortcut moves the cursor directly to the **address bar**, allowing users to quickly type in or edit the file path or web address.
 
• It is a convenient way to navigate between folders or websites without needing to click on the address bar with a mouse.
 
• This shortcut is compatible with popular web browsers like **Google Chrome**, **Microsoft Edge**, and **Mozilla Firefox**, as well as **File Explorer** in Windows.
 
• Using keyboard shortcuts like **Alt + D** enhances productivity and efficiency, especially for users who prefer keyboard navigation over a mouse.
 
• It is particularly useful in scenarios where users work with multiple tabs, folders, or websites and need to switch quickly between them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Deletes the selected file or folder**__

 __
 
• This function is typically performed using the **Delete** key or **Shift + Delete** for permanent deletion.
 
• It is not related to the **Alt + D** shortcut, as that focuses on the address bar instead of performing a delete operation.
 
 
 
• **Duplicates the current tab**__
 __
 
• Duplicating tabs can usually be done with shortcuts like **Ctrl + Shift + T** in some web browsers.
 
• The **Alt + D** shortcut does not duplicate tabs but rather focuses on the **address bar**.
 
 
 
• **Displays desktop**__
 
 
• The shortcut to display the desktop in Windows is typically **Windows + D**.
 
• The **Alt + D** shortcut does not perform this function, as its main purpose is to focus on the **address bar**.
